description: P251 STATE_TRANSITION examine-time reasoning checkpoint — shape markers for the 5 state-transition families (S1-S5). RESEARCH-ONLY, default-off, un-wired. Mirrors the P249 accounting checkpoint: it OBSERVES these shapes and emits an interrogative STATE_TRANSITION_CHECKPOINT record (8 questions + empty hypothesis); it NEVER concludes a vulnerability or emits a finding. Markers are intentionally broad (observe, don't conclude) because firing only asks a question — adjudication happens later in the existing precision pipeline. No sixth family.

S2_growable_set_unbounded_loop._comment: two-signal = a loop AND a STORAGE-set operation (grow or iterate). Catches the consume-side loop (e.g. pause iterating _liveProposals) even when the grow-side (.add) is in another function; a generic memory-array loop has no set-op so stays silent.

S3_dual_state_inconsistency._comment: tightened: only genuinely-paired status/vote vocab (dropped generic lock/unlock/enable/disable/active to avoid noise).

S4_branch_consequence_not_traced._comment: tightened: a genuine FAILURE/SHORTFALL branch (dropped generic else/return/bare-assign) AND a value-mutation.

questions: Q1: Can an attacker choose the state transition?
Q2: Can the transition be repeated?
Q3: Does the transition overwrite another user's critical state?
Q4: Does the transition grow an unbounded set or loop?
Q5: Can two incompatible states both become true?
Q6: Does a failure/shortfall branch still update state?
Q7: Does a time-window change affect existing state?
Q8: Who is harmed if this state persists?
